record.original_question: How can one characterize the possible shapes of bounded or unbounded non-convex expectation-parameter spaces that arise from non-steep exponential families?

evidence.quote: How to characterize possible shapes of non-convex expectation parameter spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{E} = \{p_\theta(x) = \exp(\langle \theta, t(x)\rangle - F(\theta))\,h(x) : \theta \in \Theta\}$ be an exponential family on a measurable space $(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$, where $t : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}^d$ is the sufficient statistic, $h \geq 0$ is a base measure density, and 
$$\Theta = \{\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d : F(\theta) := \log \int_\mathcal{X} \exp(\langle \theta, t(x)\rangle)\, h(x)\, d\mu(x) < \infty\}$$
is the natural parameter space (which is convex). The expectation parameter space is
$$M = \{\eta(\theta) := \nabla F(\theta) : \theta \in \mathrm{int}(\Theta)\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d.$$
The family $\mathcal{E}$ is called steep when $\|\nabla F(\theta_n)\| \to \infty$ for every sequence $\theta_n \in \mathrm{int}(\Theta)$ converging to a boundary point of $\Theta$; equivalently, $M$ equals the interior of the convex hull of the support of the pushforward of $\mu$ under $t$. When $\mathcal{E}$ is steep, $M$ is automatically convex; when $\mathcal{E}$ is non-steep, $M$ may fail to be convex.

Provide a complete geometric and topological characterization of the possible shapes of the expectation parameter space $M$ that can arise from non-steep exponential families, both in the bounded case and in the unbounded case. Specifically, determine which subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ are realizable as $M = \nabla F(\mathrm{int}(\Theta))$ for some non-steep exponential family.
artifact.status_search_result: General references on exponential families establish that the natural parameter space is always convex and that the expectation parameter space coincides with the interior of the convex hull of the support exactly when the family is steep. For non-steep exponential families, the expectation parameter space can be non-convex, but no general characterization of the possible shapes (bounded or unbounded) appears in the standard literature, and the question is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Exponential family - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The natural parameter space is always convex; steepness is defined via the gradient of the log-partition function blowing up at the boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Steepness is the standard property guaranteeing that the expectation parameter space equals the interior of the convex hull of the support.

status_evidence.title: Stat 8112 Lecture Notes: Asymptotics of Exponential Families
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses steep vs. non-steep exponential families and the difference between the mean value parameter space and the convex support.
status_evidence.claim: For non-steep families the mean (expectation) parameter space is a strict subset of the interior of the convex hull of the support and need not be convex.
